title: The Mouse, the Cat, and the Hawk
summary: In a granary yard, an old tabby cat was trapped in a heavy hempen net set by the miller to catch wild polecats. A field mouse, foraging for grain, approached cautiously and saw ...
full_text:
In a granary yard, an old tabby cat was trapped in a heavy hempen net set by the miller to catch wild polecats. A field mouse, foraging for grain, approached cautiously and saw that a sharp-eyed hawk was circling in the sky above, waiting to pounce upon any rodent in the open grass.

The mouse, perceiving that the hawk above was a swifter death than the trapped cat below, addressed the cat: 'O feline hunter! We are both in mortal peril: if the hawk strikes, I am devoured; and when the miller arrives, you will be drowned. If you swear a sacred covenant not to harm me, my sharp teeth can gnaw through the hempen cords around your paws, freeing you to chase the hawk away!'

The trapped cat swore a solemn oath of peace.

The mouse gnawed with furious speed through the thick ropes. The moment the cat broke free, it leaped with claws extended, driving the swooping hawk away into the clouds!

The cat then returned to the barn, purring sweetly, and sat outside the mouse’s burrow: 'Come forth, heroic friend! Let us embrace and live as brothers forever.'

The wise mouse remained safely inside its deep hole, peeking through a narrow crack, and answered: 'Brother, I honor our alliance, and I thank you for driving the hawk away. But an alliance born of shared emergency ends when the danger passes. Nature is nature, and I shall keep this stone wall between your claws and my fur!'

The mouse survived, demonstrating that wisdom cooperates in crisis, but maintains prudent boundaries in peace.
moral: Adversaries must cooperate against a shared mortal peril, but prudence must outlive temporary alliances.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Mouse and the Cat"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
